newsitem.title: CHILE: New Chile environment rules push up costs - gov't.
newsitem.headline: New Chile environment rules push up costs - gov't.

text.p: The costs of investing in new projects in Chile will rise by 2-5 percent as new environment laws will force companies to buy cleaner, more expensive technology, said a top government official.

"It would not be wrong to think what will happen in Chile will be the same as in other countries, where investment costs have risen by 3-5 percent as firms buy cleaner technology to comply with the rules," said Vivianne Blanlot, director of the National Environment Commission.
These higher costs should be offset by lower operating expenses and greater oppportunities to trade with countries with high environmental standards, she told a news conference.
"If laws are more rigorous, countries have quicker access to other markets," said Blanlot.
"I believe that the economic effect, although difficult to predict, will be positive and not negative on investment in the medium term."
Environmental impact studies will be compulsory for all new projects once the latest regulations are published by the government Thursday.
The new rules are unlikely to have much impact on most projects as companies have been preparing the reports voluntarily for several years, she said.
"Projects which meet the law could not suffer modifications to be approved. What is extra is that companies will have to carry out broader studies than they have been used to," said Blanlot.
